candidates.text: When dispatching a staged subagent (Engineer/Quality Engineer) via the Agent/SendMessage tooling, a background '[handback-send-enforce]' mechanism can inject forced-handback messages into the agent's own turn sequence before the orchestrator's real reply arrives, causing the agent to correctly self-block per its own bounded-rejection rule even though neither the orchestrator nor the agent violated the documented protocol. Treat a resulting self-blocked report with zero real command evidence as a continuity_broken event (not a product/verification verdict), retain it honestly, and dispatch a genuinely fresh agent instance for that phase rather than trying to resume or promote the phantom-caused blocked report as canonical.

Before designing a new mechanism for live_cli.py (the live orchestrator bridge), check whether harness/orchestrator/core.py's deterministic engine already solved the same problem -- it often has, since core.py is deterministically tested first and its own internal helpers (e.g. _validate_and_promote's filename override, driving the repair-round f'{stem}.repair-{n}.json' convention) can usually be extracted into a shared evidence_io.py function and reused by both, rather than inventing a parallel design. This closed the run-20260917-logicrepair-002 gap (FACT-20260918-PROMOTE-NO-REPAIR-PATH) cleanly: core.py already had the exact convention, live_cli.py just needed to expose it.
